audit.whatIsWrong: The chart tokens are right and both layers agree, but three of the full-layer 'why' lines were generic boilerplate that contradicted their own row: level 1 said 'he literally cannot touch you' on a row scored Sion, first item promised melting tanks on an even row, and 2+ items promised a teamfight nightmare on a row scored Sion.
audit.why: Content whys[0], whys[5] and whys[6] already say the opposite of those three lines, so the page argued with itself on every stage where Sion is not losing.
audit.corrected: All three whys rewritten to match their side; no chart tokens moved, since packet, full and content already agree row for row.

audit.whatIsWrong: The 2+ items spike was credited only to 'HP pool and zombie passive'; the page never says what Glory in Death actually does to you.
audit.why: The reanimation attacks rapidly, heals him, and deals bonus damage based on your maximum health — so killing Sion starts a second fight, and Grievous Wounds on the corpse is the item answer nobody stated.
audit.corrected: late now names the healing and the anti-heal requirement.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabrications. dosFull[0].d and report[5].t told you to 'break the channel' on Decimating Smash, and wants.foe[1] describes an 'E shield-break poke'. Sion's Q is a chargeable swing, not a channel with an interrupt listed anywhere in Riot's text, and Roar of the Slayer breaks no shields — it slows and reduces armour, and knocks a minion back through everyone behind it.
audit.why: Telling a Lillia to interrupt a charge is advice she cannot act on — she has no interrupt before 6 — and it hides the thing that matters: only a FULL charge knocks up and stuns. A short charge is damage you can walk through.
audit.corrected: Both strings rewritten around charge length and the 10/9/8/7/6s cooldown; the E restated as armour shred plus minion knockback.

audit.whatIsWrong: early, mid and late are written in the first person, and diff reads FAVOURED where every other Lillia page uses FAV.
audit.why: Voice mismatch, and a diff token the renderer may not recognise.
audit.corrected: All three converted to second person; diff set to FAV.

edits.before: Q's outer ring on his last-hits plus the passive speed means he literally cannot touch you at level 1.
edits.after: He shoves with Roar of the Slayer and a full-charge Q threatens a knockup before you own a kite chain.

edits.before: Liandry's spike — Dream Dust plus the burn melts juggernauts and tanks alike while you jog circles around them.
edits.after: Liandry's bites his HP stack, but Soul Furnace's shield and one full-charge Q still flip any trade — even.

edits.before: You're a teamfight nightmare now: sleep two, kite the rest, and let the burn do the bookkeeping.
edits.after: Two tank items and Glory in Death shrug your burn; a fog-charged Q ends you. Roam, don't duel.

edits.before: Charged knockup — break the channel or sidestep the slam. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Only a full charge knocks up — sidestep the arc, then punish the 10s cooldown at rank 1.

edits.before: Sion spends Decimating Smash (Stun) early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Decimating Smash is 10s at rank 1 — once he swings and misses, walk in and ring him twice.

edits.before: Track Sion’s Decimating Smash (Stun): Charged knockup — break the channel or sidestep the slam. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Decimating Smash: only a full charge knocks up and stuns — a short charge is just damage, so read the wind-up length, not the cast.

edits.before: Level 1 is his — Sion can shove with E and his charged Q threatens a knockup before I have a kite chain, so I just farm Blooming Blows from range and concede the opening. The moment I hit 2-3 it flips: my second Q sweetspot plus the Swirlseed slow starts the Dream Dust burn, and the stacking move speed from Q makes me uncatchable for an immobile tank. The only thing that catches me is a fully charged Q, so never stand still in front of him while he winds it up — sidestep the airborne and let the burn tick.
edits.after: Level 1 is his — Roar of the Slayer shoves the wave and a charged Q threatens a knockup before you have a kite chain, so farm Blooming Blows from range and concede the opening. At 2-3 it flips: the second Q sweetspot plus the Swirlseed slow starts the Dream Dust burn, and stacking move speed makes you uncatchable for an immobile tank. Only a fully charged Q catches you — a short charge is damage, nothing more — so read the wind-up length, never stand still in front of it, and let the burn tick.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are my best lane window: full-rank Q, the Dream Dust DoT compounding, and enough mana to grind him down means every step he takes to last-hit feeds the burn, and his W shield can't soak a sustained DoT forever. Keep hitting the outer Q sweetspot, weave E slows, and kite in circles he can't answer. At 6 my Lilting Lullaby is a real setup if I've stacked Dream Dust on him — but the sleep is delayed and his charged Q is the single button that can knock me up mid-kite, so bait that Q out before I commit the ult or a jungler gank.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your best lane window: full-rank Q and the compounding Dream Dust DoT mean every step he takes to last-hit feeds the burn, and Soul Furnace's shield can't soak a sustained DoT forever — note it only deals its damage on a reactivation three seconds later. Keep hitting the outer sweetspot, weave Swirlseed slows, and kite in circles. At 6 Lilting Lullaby is a real setup once Dream Dust is on him, but the sleep is delayed and a charged Q is the one button that catches you — bait it out before you commit the ult or a gank.

edits.before: This is where Sion reclaims it. Once he has two tank items his HP pool and zombie passive let him shrug my DoT in a teamfight — I can't burn through that much effective health fast enough, and a charged Q out of fog one-shot-locks my squishy, button-less body. So I don't try to out-DoT a full-tank Sion late; I cash my 4-to-first-item tempo into roams, objectives, and picks on his squishier teammates with R, and I never facecheck a brush where a charged Q is waiting. Win the map before his tankiness decides the game.
edits.after: This is where Sion reclaims it. With two tank items his HP pool shrugs your DoT in a teamfight, and Glory in Death means killing him only starts a second fight — the reanimation attacks fast, heals him, and hits for a share of your max health, so someone on your team needs Grievous Wounds ready for the corpse. A charged Q out of fog locks your button-less body outright. Cash your 4-to-first-item tempo into roams, objectives and picks with R, and never facecheck a brush where a charge is waiting.

edits.before: Use his W shield and E shield-break poke to soak your DoT and shove you off the wave
edits.after: Use Soul Furnace's shield and Roar of the Slayer's armour shred to soak your DoT and shove you off

notes: The chart needed no flips here — packet, full and content already matched — so the whole fix was prose that contradicted the chart. Roar of the Slayer's minion-knockback line (it shoves a minion back through everyone behind it) is real but only matters when you are standing behind your own wave; I left it off the page rather than spend length on a rare case. As on the Shen page, I did not use Lillia's 'terrain' flag to claim Swirlseed can block Unstoppable Onslaught — Riot's Swirlseed text does not support it.
